description: `config.aria: false` is a statement about the whole drawing — "a boolean flag indicating if ARIA default attributes should be included for marks and guides" — and a guide has to carry it on itself, because a renderer reading the specification a guide at a time has nothing else to tell it that the chart it belongs to is not being described. `assembleAxis` writes it as the last word of the main axis: `{scale, orient, grid: false, ...title, ...axis, ...(config.aria === false ? {aria: false} : {}), zindex}`. This compiler wrote nothing, so a document that takes its charts out of the accessibility tree left every axis in it announcing itself to a screen reader as an axis. Three things about where that spread sits. It is **after** `...axis`, so it overrules what the axis itself said: the horizontal axis here asks for `aria: true` and comes out `false`, which is right, since an axis cannot opt back into a tree the chart is not in. It is on the **main** axis only — the gridlines are `aria: false` whatever the theme says, `assembleAxis` writing that one unconditionally in its grid arm, because a grid is a repetition of the axis beside it and reading it out twice tells a listener nothing. And it is the axis's own rule rather than a shared one: the legend's twin in `assembleLegend` is guarded by `legend.aria == undefined`, so a legend that asks for `aria: true` keeps it where an axis does not. The colour key here must not change — it states nothing, so it takes the `false` it would have taken before this rule existed, and its presence says the two guides were not made to share a reading.
